question.value: How does the magnetic field structure in the Class 0 protostar B335 behave on a 100 au scale, and is it consistent with MHD simulations with aligned or misaligned magnetic field and rotational axis?

evidence.quote: To observationally investigate the effects of the magnetic field on the disk formation in B335, we conducted ALMA polarimetric observations at an angular resolution of 0.2$''$ (20 au)
consisting of 13 successful executions (project code: 2015.1.01018.S)
The observations were conducted with the full polarization mode and at the frequency ranges of 335.5–339.5 GHz and 347.5–351.5 GHz with a total bandwidth of 8 GHz.
at the frequency ranges of 335.5–339.5 GHz and 347.5–351.5 GHz with a total bandwidth of 8 GHz

The achieved synthesized beam is $0.19\ensuremath{''} \times 0.17\ensuremath{''}$.
The noise level in the Stokes *I* image is 40 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$, and it is 9 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$ in the Stokes *Q* and *U* images.
The on-source integration time was 7.4 hours.

findings_qualitative.value: B-field changes from ordered pinched on 1000 au to complicated, asymmetric structures within 100 au, connecting to the center along the equatorial plane and 40-60 deg off it

evidence.quote: the magnetic field connects to the center along the equatorial plane as well as along the directions which are $\sim$40$\ensuremath{^\circ}$–60$\ensuremath{^\circ}$ from the equatorial plane
